title: Argument tree (confrontatie-as)
description: Output contract for the bipolariteit.org argumentenboom pipeline (issue #252): a topic-independent set of nodes plus typed relations between them, produced in two stages -- a structuring pass selects nodes/relations, then a redactie pass judges each relation in its own isolated call with a single neutral, functional question ('does the premise argument demonstrably engage the target argument's core point?' for conflict, 'does the premise argument give an explicit reason to believe the target?' for support) -- never a validity/quality judgement, and never from an assigned pro/contra role. A relation the check answers 'no' to is dropped before this schema is validated; it never appears here. See pipeline/prompts/boomredactie_rebuttal_detection.md and pipeline/prompts/boomredactie_support_check.md, and issue #252 for why the earlier two-sided-review design (weak_link from reviewer disagreement) was replaced -- it turned out not to discriminate between relations at all, converging on a single label regardless of content. The relation shape below is the tree-specific superset of pipeline/schemas/argument_relations.schema.json's AIF-core relation (thema added) -- duplicated rather than $ref'd across files so each schema stays independently valid without a schema registry.

nodes.description: The selected subset of arguments that make up the tree.

argument_id.description: id of the argument, must exist in the source database.

gist.description: Very short (3-4 words) summary for the tree display. Never a paraphrase that adds facts not in the quote itself.

samenvatting.description: 1-2 sentence readable summary of this node together with everything that supports it, or null for a leaf node whose quote is already short enough.

relations.description: Typed relations between nodes (AIF core: support = RA-node, conflict = CA-node). A support relation with one premise is a simple 'kid'; with several premises it is a coordinative group. A conflict relation anchors a band in the tree.

items.description: One RA-node (support) or CA-node (conflict): premise_argument_ids feed the relation, target_argument_id is the argument being supported or attacked.

relation_type.description: support = RA-node (premises logically back up the target). conflict = CA-node (premises rebut or undermine the target).

target_argument_id.description: id of the argument being supported or attacked.

premise_argument_ids.description: ids of the arguments that feed the relation. More than 1 item = a coordinative group: the premises only carry the target jointly, not individually.

thema.description: Short (max ~8 words), neutral title naming the actual point of contention -- only set on conflict relations, becomes the band title. Never a fact/number/judgement, and never just the two gists glued together.

scheme.description: Refinement of relation_type. For conflict: 'direct_rebuttal' (explicitly rebuts the same point), 'thematic' (touches the same sub-topic, no direct rebuttal), or 'frame_shift' (shifts the discussion to a different value/framing instead of rebutting the point itself). For support: a Walton argumentation-scheme name if one clearly applies, otherwise null.

reden.description: One short, case-specific sentence from the redactie pass justifying why this relation passed its neutral engagement check (see the schema-level description) -- never a generic restatement of the relation_type, always grounded in what the two arguments actually say.

sterkte.description: Score (0.0-1.0) van de redactiecheck voor hoe sterk premise en target elkaar raken -- de relatie is alleen opgenomen omdat deze een gekozen drempel haalde (default 0.5, zie merge_engagement_checks). Ontbreekt bij bomen die zijn gebouwd vóór de invoering van deze score (issue #254 vervolg), toen de check nog een booleaanse ja/nee gaf.

coordinatieve_groepen.description: Argument groups that are only ever shown as a bundle outside the confrontatie-as (never a band side): several arguments that independently make a similar point, without one supporting another and without being part of any conflict relation.

label.description: Short (max ~6 words), neutral summary of the shared point.

twijfelachtige_classificaties.description: Arguments encountered whose existing pro/contra stance looks clearly wrong. Reported, never silently corrected or excluded from the source data.
